title: Butternut Squash Soup
subtitle: Smooth roasted squash soup
excerpt: Butternut squash roasted until caramelised, then blended with stock into a velvety smooth soup. A pinch of chilli and a swirl of cream to serve.

recipe.sourceNotes: Roasted butternut squash soup is a staple of contemporary British and American home cooking. Roasting the squash before blending, rather than simmering it directly in stock, was popularised in the 1990s and gives a sweeter, deeper flavour.

recipeTools.notes: Large enough to hold the squash in a single layer.

content.text: Butternut squash soup is made by roasting the squash until the edges caramelise, which deepens its flavour compared to boiling. The roasted flesh is blended with stock into a smooth, velvety soup with a natural sweetness. A little chilli lifts it and stops it being too cloying.

items.preparation: peeled, deseeded, cut into 3 cm chunks

content.text: Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Spread the squash and onion over a large roasting tin. Tuck in the unpeeled garlic cloves. Drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and chilli flakes, and toss to coat.
Roast for 40 to 45 minutes until the squash is completely tender and the edges are golden and caramelised. The garlic should be very soft inside its skin.
Squeeze the roasted garlic from its skin into a large saucepan. Add the squash, onion, and the stock. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes.
Blend the soup with a stick blender until completely smooth. Adjust the consistency with more stock if needed. Taste for salt.
Ladle into bowls, swirl over a little cream, and add the fried sage leaves if using.
